info.bio:
There is more than one band with the name Brick. A funk/jazz band from Atlanta, GA, USA, a hardcore band from Baltimore, MD, USA, a hard rock band from Finland, a noise rock band from Sweden, a death metal band from Saint Paul, MN, USA and a heavy metal band from Sweden.

1) Brick was an Atlanta band that created a successful merger of funk and jazz in the '70s they called "dazz." Brick's roster included lead vocalist/saxophonist/flutist Jimmy Brown; guitarist/bassist/vocalist Regi Hargis Hickman; lead singer Ray Ransom

scenes.name: La industria del disco y la muerte del R&B
scenes.book: Funk: The Music, the People, and the Rhythm of the One
scenes.author: Rickey Vincent
scenes.desc: Las emisoras negras se volvieron «urban contemporary» (WBLS en Nueva York, KSOL en San Francisco), con menos DJ negros y música menos negra; según Nelson George (The Death of Rhythm and Blues), Millie Jackson o Cameo pasaron a ser «demasiado negros»: un suicidio cultural. El «Harvard Report» de CBS trató el soul como producto; Neil Bogart (Casablanca: Donna Summer, Kiss, Village People, Parliament) inventó el bombo y las ventas imaginarias, y los independientes de promoción, la payola. Los artistas pagaban su promoción, había que llegar al oro para ganar algo y las tiendas pequeñas desaparecieron. Quien se oponía, como Jack «the Rapper» Gibson, era tachado de radical. El único consuelo: la América blanca también le declaró la guerra al disco. La Disco Demolition del estadio de los White Sox (12 de julio de 1979) acabó en disturbios; pero para el público rock «disco» pasó a significar toda música negra y el funk de finales de los setenta (P-Funk, Slave, Brick, Bar-Kays) quedó condenado con él.

scenes.name: Monster funk: la tercera dinastía
scenes.book: Funk: The Music, the People, and the Rhythm of the One
scenes.author: Rickey Vincent
scenes.desc: El fantasma del disco solo intensificó el funk de baile de los verdaderos funkers: la Edad de Oro del baile y la cima del movimiento. La influencia de P-Funk llenó las bandas de capas, viajes espaciales y personajes («Captain Quick Draw», «Big Chief Funkum», «Jupiter», «Wonder Worm» de Captain Sky, «Galaxy» de War, «Long Stroke» de ADC Band). Brick, quinteto de Atlanta, inventó con «Dazz» (1976) el «disco-jazz», con el bajo de Ray Ransom y la flauta funky de Jimmy Brown; nunca fue banda de disco. El Medio Oeste fue el semillero: Slave, de Dayton (Steve Washington, sobrino de un Ohio Player, el bajo de Mark Adams, la guitarra de Drac Hicks), con «Slide» y luego la voz de Steve Arrington; Sun («Radiation Level»); Lakeside, empaquetados por SOLAR con un disfraz por disco («It’s All the Way Live», «Fantastic Voyage»). De Vallejo, Con Funk Shun («Ffun»). «Con el funk no hay reglas», decía Washington.

mentions.author: Rickey Vincent
mentions.text: …your ego trip can take you as far as you want to go. BRICK Just as the major funk bands were scoring huge hits in 1976, the Atlanta-based quintet Brick blasted onto the radio with a monstrous slice of “disco-jazz,” known as “Dazz.” Somehow reflecting a sound with the richness of southern New Orleans–style rhythm and blues, as well as a heightened jazz sensibility, combined with smash-mouth funk chops, Brick blasted into the higher echelons of The Funk. His ability to jump from saxophone to trumpet to flute was a visual as well as musical experience, and his locked-tight backup brought Brick instant success. “Dazz,” the album title cut “Good High,” the instrumental “Brick City,” and the incredible follow-up monster jams “Dusic,” “Ain’t Gonna Hurt Nobody,” and “(We Don’t Wanna Sit Down) We Wanna Git Down” surged Brick to the verge of superstardom by 1977. mentions.author: Rickey Vincent
mentions.text: …and intricate interplay. “It ain’t gonna hurt nobody/to get on down/don’t stop me/and I won’t stop you.” And while it makes no sense to say that Brick lacked any essential qualities, the absence of a charismatic lead singer kept the band somewhat anonymous as the years went by. Their third album, two years later, although noble in its grounded, blues-funk ideals, was a tragic, quirky disappointment, for Brick was one of the last bands that fans believed could master the pop formulas and still come with The Bomb. They kept their funk, but went down for the count.
